$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(arsinh\,(\frac{x-3}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{x-3}{3})}^{2}+1}}\cdot {(\frac{x-3}{3})}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{9}+1}}\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{\frac{(x-3)^{2}+9}{9}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{(x-3)^{2}+9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}-6x+9)+9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-6x+18}}.\end{aligned}
$$
